transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess I came in because I’ve been feeling… more thrown off than I expected lately. I’ve been trying to clean up my image and my routine because of some arts board stuff I’m involved with, and I thought that would make me feel more organized, or at least more together. But instead I’ve just been really tense and kind of down about it.

I’m still doing the basics, like I’m not completely falling apart or anything, but I keep dropping these smaller things that I normally care about. Like fair planning notes, or design drafts I meant to finish or revise, and then when I realize I’ve let something slip, I feel guilty and embarrassed. And instead of just catching up like a normal person, I end up canceling plans or avoiding people because I feel behind and don’t want to deal with it. It’s just been this loop, and I don’t really like how I’m handling it.
Can you describe how often you’ve felt down or depressed lately, and whether this feeling seems to come and go or stays with you most of the time?

It’s not like it’s every single second of the day, but it’s been happening a lot more than I’m used to. It sort of comes in waves, I guess. Like, if I’m just getting through basic stuff, I can seem okay, and I can still do the minimum things I need to do. But then I’ll remember something small I let slide, like notes for the fair planning or a design draft I meant to clean up, and it just sinks my mood.

And then it kind of sticks for a while because I start feeling guilty and embarrassed, like I should be handling things better, especially since the whole point was to get my image and routine together for the arts board stuff. Instead, I feel tense and disappointed in myself. So I’ll end up canceling plans or avoiding people because I feel behind, and that makes me feel even worse.

So I wouldn’t say I’m completely depressed all day, nonstop, but it’s been frequent enough that it feels like it’s hanging around in the background most days lately.
Have you noticed that you’re not getting as much enjoyment or interest out of things you usually like doing, like your art or planning for the board?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that, honestly. I don’t think it’s like I’ve stopped liking art or the board planning, because I still care about those things a lot. Sometimes maybe too much, which is part of why I get so worked up when I feel like I’m not doing them right.

It’s more like… when I sit down to do something I normally enjoy, I’m already thinking about what I’m behind on or how it’s going to look to other people, so it doesn’t feel as easy or fun in the moment. But I wouldn’t say I have no interest in it. I still want to do the drafts, and I still want the planning to go well. It’s just been harder to relax into it, if that makes sense.
Have you noticed that you're feeling more tired or run down lately, even if you're not doing anything particularly strenuous?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I wouldn’t say I’ve clearly noticed being physically exhausted in some big way, like where I can’t get through the day or anything. It’s more that I feel kind of mentally worn out from thinking about everything, if that makes sense.

Like, I’ll be sitting there not doing anything that demanding, but my head is still going over what I forgot, what I should be fixing, whether I’m making a bad impression, and that can make me feel sort of drained. But I don’t know if that’s the same as being tired or run down in the way you mean. I’m still able to do basic things, so it’s not like I’m constantly wiped out. It’s just… I feel worn out by the stress of it, more than by actual activity.
Have you found that activities you usually enjoy, like your art or planning for the board, feel flat or uninteresting, even if you still care about them?

Yeah, sort of, but I don’t think it’s that they feel completely uninteresting, exactly. I still care about them a lot, maybe that’s why it’s been bothering me so much. It’s more like since I started trying to get my image and routine together for the arts board stuff, everything has felt heavier than I expected.

Like, I’ll sit down meaning to work on fair planning notes or clean up a design draft, and instead of feeling excited or focused, I notice all the little things I’ve dropped or let slide. Then I start feeling guilty, like I should’ve already handled it, and embarrassed that I’m not keeping up the way I wanted to. So the thing itself isn’t flat because I don’t care — it’s more like the stress gets in the way of enjoying it.

I’m still doing the basic things I need to do, but I keep missing these smaller things that actually matter to me, and then I get tense and down about it. Sometimes instead of catching up, I’ll cancel plans or avoid people because I feel behind, which just makes the whole thing feel worse. So… not uninteresting exactly, but definitely not enjoyable in the normal way.
Can you think of a time recently when you felt genuinely interested or pleased while working on your art or the board planning, even for a little while?

Yeah… I can think of little moments, I guess. Like if I’m actually in the middle of a design draft and I stop thinking about whether I’m behind or whether it’s good enough, there are still parts where I’m like, “Oh, that looks right,” or I get interested in fixing one small piece of it. So it’s not like that feeling is totally gone.

But it doesn’t last very long lately. Since I started trying to clean up my image and get my routine together for the arts board stuff, I’ve been more tense and kind of down than I expected. I’ll start out trying to work on fair planning notes or a draft, and then I notice some little thing I dropped that I normally would’ve cared about, and it kind of ruins the good feeling. Then I feel guilty, like I should have already handled it, and instead of catching up I’ll sometimes cancel plans or avoid dealing with it for a bit.

So yes, there are still small moments where I feel interested or pleased, but they get crowded out pretty quickly by the stress around it.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the flip side, feeling restless or fidgety in a way that’s not typical for you?

I don’t think so, not in a really obvious way. I haven’t had anyone tell me I’m talking slower or moving strangely, and I don’t feel like I’m dragging physically, if that’s what you mean.

Restless… maybe a little in the sense that I can have trouble just settling down with things, like I’ll shift around or get up and check something, but I’m not sure that’s unusual for me or if I’m just noticing it more because I’m already stressed about how I’m handling everything. It’s not like I’m pacing all day or can’t sit still at all. And I don’t think I’m speaking slowly or anything like that.

So I guess my answer is mostly no, or at least I haven’t noticed a clear change there.
Have you found yourself not caring about things you usually care about, even your art or the planning for the board, not even wanting to do them at all?

Not exactly like I don’t care at all, no. That’s the frustrating part — I do still care about my art and the board planning. I think if I genuinely didn’t care, it might almost feel simpler, but I do care, and then I feel worse when I’m not keeping up with it the way I think I should.

What brought me in is more that since I started trying to clean up my image and get my routine together for the arts board stuff, I’ve felt more tense and down than I expected. I’m still doing the basic things, like I’m not just completely abandoning everything, but I keep dropping these smaller things that I normally would stay on top of — fair planning notes, design drafts, little follow-ups or pieces of prep — and then I get this guilty feeling, like, “Why didn’t I just handle that?”

And then sometimes instead of catching up, I cancel plans or avoid people because I feel behind or embarrassed. So it’s not that I don’t want the art or the board work at all. It’s more like wanting to do it is still there, but the stress around it makes me pull back or freeze up.

Can you tell me if you’ve noticed a change in how you feel about doing your art or working on the board planning — like, even if you still care about them, do they feel less satisfying or enjoyable than they used to?

Yeah… I think they do feel less satisfying, but not because I stopped caring about them. It’s more like the enjoyment gets mixed up with pressure now.

Like, before, if I was working on a design draft or making notes for fair planning, I could kind of get absorbed in it and feel like, okay, this is why I like doing this. Lately, since I’ve been trying to clean up my image and get my routine together for the arts board stuff, I go into it already feeling tense, like I’m trying to prove I can keep everything under control. So even when I do the basic things, there’s this background stress.

And then I’ll notice I dropped some small thing I normally would care about — like a planning note I meant to finish, or a draft I should’ve revised — and instead of the work feeling satisfying, it turns into guilt. I start thinking, “Why didn’t I just handle that earlier?” Then sometimes I’ll cancel plans or avoid catching up because I feel embarrassed or behind, which obviously makes it worse.

So, yes, I still care about the art and the board planning, but they don’t feel as cleanly enjoyable as they used to. They feel heavier right now.
Has there been a time in the last few weeks when something you used to really enjoy, like your art or the board planning, didn’t feel good or interesting to you at all, even for a little while?

I’m not sure I can point to a moment where it felt like I had no interest at all. That sounds a little stronger than what I’ve noticed.

There have definitely been times where I sat down to do something art-related or board-planning-related and it just didn’t feel good in the way it normally does. Like I’d open up a draft or look at planning notes and instead of feeling curious or excited, I’d feel kind of tired of it before I even started — not physically tired exactly, just like, “Ugh, I don’t want to deal with this right now.” But even then, I don’t think it was that I didn’t care or that it had no meaning to me. It was more that I was already tense about it, so the interest got buried under that.

So… maybe yes in small patches, if you mean it didn’t feel enjoyable for a little while. But if you mean completely blank, like I felt nothing toward it or didn’t care whether I ever did it again, then no, I don’t think that’s happened. It’s more that it feels heavy and pressured, not totally uninteresting.

In the past few weeks, have there been times when you couldn’t feel any pleasure or interest in things, even things you usually enjoy like your art or the board planning — like nothing felt good or meaningful at all?

I don’t think I’ve had it where nothing felt good or meaningful at all. That sounds more absolute than what I’ve been experiencing.

It’s more like… things can feel dulled or weighed down, especially with the art and board planning, but there’s still something there. Like even if I’m frustrated or tense, I still know I care about it, and sometimes I can still get a little satisfaction from doing part of it, even if it’s not the same as before. I wouldn’t say it’s this total blankness where I can’t feel any pleasure in anything.

So, no, not really “nothing felt good or meaningful at all.” It’s more that the good feeling is harder to get to, if that makes sense.
Have you felt a persistent loss of energy or felt fatigued even when you haven’t been doing anything physically or mentally demanding?

I don’t think I’d call it a persistent loss of energy, no. I mean, I have moments where I feel kind of drained, but when I really think about it, it usually seems tied to being tense or overwhelmed by what I’m trying to handle, not like this constant fatigue that’s there no matter what.

Like, if I’m just sitting around and nothing much is happening, I don’t usually feel physically wiped out for no reason. It’s more that I can feel mentally sort of weighed down when I’m thinking about everything I should be doing, and then I might move slower or put things off. But I’m not sure that’s the same as having no energy even when nothing demanding is going on.

So… not really in a persistent way. I haven’t noticed that as a main thing.
Have you been doing less of your usual activities, like your art or spending time with people, because you just don’t feel like it or it doesn’t seem worth the effort?

Yeah… I think that’s actually closer to what’s been happening. Not like I’ve stopped everything or I’m just lying around doing nothing, because I am still doing the basics. I’m getting through the necessary stuff. But I’ve definitely been doing less of the smaller things I usually keep up with, especially around the arts board work.

Like, since I started trying to clean up my image and get my routine together for that, I expected to feel more organized or proud of myself, but instead I’ve been more tense and kind of down than I thought I would be. And then I’ll avoid little things that normally matter to me — fair planning notes, design drafts, things like that. They’re not impossible tasks, but they start to feel like this whole pile of pressure, and then I don’t do them, or I do the absolute minimum.

And with people… yeah, sometimes I cancel plans, but it’s not exactly because I don’t care about seeing them. It’s more like I feel guilty that I’m behind, and then instead of catching up or letting myself go out, I just cancel because I feel like I shouldn’t be doing anything fun until I’ve fixed everything. Which doesn’t really help, because then I’m alone and still not catching up. So yes, I guess I have been doing less, but it feels more tied to stress and guilt than just not caring.

Have you found yourself avoiding starting or finishing tasks, even small ones you normally wouldn’t think twice about, because you feel overwhelmed by what you’ve already let slip or guilty about not doing them sooner?

Yes… that’s probably one of the main things, honestly. It’s not usually that the task itself is huge. It can be something small, like writing up fair planning notes or working on a design draft, things I normally would just sit down and do without making it into a whole ordeal.

But lately, since I’ve been trying to sort of clean up my image and get into a better routine for the arts board stuff, it’s like I expected that to make me feel more together, and instead I’ve felt more tense and kind of down about it. Then if I let one little thing slip, it doesn’t stay little in my head. It turns into, “Well, now I’m behind, and now people are going to notice, and now I should have done this days ago,” and then starting it feels worse because I’m already guilty.

So I’m still doing the basic things I have to do, but I keep dropping these smaller things that I actually do care about. And then I’ll do something like cancel plans because I feel like I don’t deserve to go out or I shouldn’t be having fun until I’ve caught up. But then I don’t always catch up anyway, so it’s just me sitting there feeling bad about both things. It’s frustrating because I know the task would probably take less time than all the avoiding, but I still get stuck.
Have you found yourself feeling guilty or worthless, even about small things you’ve let slip, to the point where it really weighs on you?

Yeah… I wouldn’t say I feel worthless exactly, or at least that word feels a little strong, but guilty, yes. Definitely guilty. And it can be over things that, when I say them out loud, sound kind of small.

Like with the arts board stuff, that’s really why I came in. Since I started trying to sort of clean up my image and get my routine in better shape, I thought I’d feel more on top of things, but instead I’ve been more tense and down than I expected. I’m still doing the basics, so it’s not like everything has fallen apart, but I keep letting these little things slip that I normally care about — fair planning notes, design drafts, those kinds of things.

And then once I’ve let something sit too long, it weighs on me way more than it probably should. I’ll think, “Why didn’t I just do that earlier?” or “Now it’s going to look like I don’t care,” and then I feel guilty enough that I avoid people or cancel plans instead of just catching up. Which is stupid, because canceling doesn’t even mean I actually get the work done. Sometimes I just sit there feeling bad about not doing the work and also feeling bad about canceling.

So, yes, the guilt part is there. It’s not constant self-hatred or anything, but it does really sit on me and make small things feel bigger than they are.
Have you ever felt that life wasn’t worth living or had thoughts about harming yourself, even just briefly, because of how guilty or down you’ve been feeling?

No… no, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve felt really guilty and kind of down, like I said, and sometimes I get stuck in that loop where everything feels heavier than it should. But I haven’t been thinking that life isn’t worth living, and I haven’t had thoughts about hurting myself.

It’s more like I get frustrated with myself, or embarrassed, or I feel like I’ve messed up something small and made it into this huge thing. But it doesn’t go to that place of wanting to harm myself. It’s uncomfortable and upsetting, but not in that way.
Have you found yourself feeling anxious or worried about tasks or responsibilities, even when there isn’t an immediate deadline or clear consequence for not doing them?

Yes, I think so. It’s not always even because there’s a real deadline right in front of me, which is part of what makes it feel so ridiculous. Like, with the arts board things, I came in because since I started trying to clean up my image a bit and get myself into a better routine, I expected I’d feel calmer or more organized. But instead I’ve been more tense and kind of down than I expected.

I’ll have something like fair planning notes or a design draft in the back of my mind, and even if nobody has said, “This has to be done today,” I’m still worried about it. It’s like it sits there making noise in my head. I’m still doing the basic things I need to do, so it’s not like I’ve completely stopped functioning, but I keep dropping these smaller things I normally care about. And then once I’ve let one slip, I start feeling guilty before there’s even a clear consequence.

Then I’ll do this thing where instead of just sitting down and catching up, I cancel plans or avoid doing something normal because I feel like I shouldn’t be doing anything else until I’ve fixed it. But then I don’t always fix it, so the worry just keeps hanging around. It’s not even always logical — it’s more like I feel responsible for being behind before anyone else has even noticed.
Have you noticed that you're feeling anxious or worried about tasks or responsibilities most days, even when there isn't a clear reason or deadline pushing you to feel that way?

Yeah… most days, I think that’s fair to say. It’s not like every single minute, but it’s there a lot, kind of running in the background.

Since I started trying to clean up my image and get into a better routine with the arts board stuff, I thought I’d feel more put together, but I’ve actually been more tense and down than I expected. And the weird part is I’m still doing the basics — I’m not completely dropping everything — but I keep missing these smaller things that I normally care about, like fair planning notes or design drafts.

Then even if there isn’t some hard deadline, I start worrying about it anyway. It feels like, “I should have done that already,” or, “If I don’t fix this, people are going to think I don’t care.” And then I get guilty, and instead of just catching up, I’ll cancel plans or avoid people because I feel like I shouldn’t be doing anything else until I deal with it. But then sometimes I still don’t deal with it, so it just sits there and makes me feel worse.

So yeah, I’d say it’s most days lately. Not always for a clear reason, but it still feels like pressure.
Have you felt down or in a low mood on most days lately, even if it wasn't constant throughout the entire day?

Yeah… I think so. Not like I wake up every single morning and it’s just nonstop the whole day, but most days lately there’s been at least some part of the day where I feel low or kind of weighed down.

It started standing out more after I tried to clean up my image a bit and get more serious about my routine with the arts board stuff. I thought doing that would make me feel better, like more organized or more in control, but instead I’ve been more tense and down than I expected. I’m still doing the basic things I have to do, so it’s not like I’m completely falling apart, but I keep letting little things slide that I normally do care about, like fair planning notes or design drafts.

And then when I realize I’ve dropped something, I feel guilty, and that makes my mood sink more. Sometimes instead of just sitting down and catching up, I’ll cancel plans or avoid doing something else because I feel like I shouldn’t be allowed to relax or go out until I’ve fixed it. But then I don’t always fix it right away, so I just end up feeling worse.

So… yeah, I’d say I’ve been feeling down most days, even if it comes and goes.

Have you noticed that you feel anxious or worried about a variety of things, not just specific tasks or responsibilities, and that this happens more often than not even when there isn’t an obvious reason?

I’m not totally sure I’d say it’s about a variety of things, exactly. I mean, it can feel kind of general once I’m already worked up, like I’ll be tense and then everything feels harder to think about, but when I try to trace it back, it usually seems connected to something I feel I’m supposed to be handling.

So… I don’t know if I’m worried out of nowhere about lots of unrelated things. It’s more like once one responsibility is sitting in my head, it spreads into this overall uneasy feeling, and then I start second-guessing myself. But I wouldn’t want to make it sound like I’m just worrying about everything all the time for no reason. I’m not sure that’s quite right.
